title: My old UI kits were static PNGs. This one comes alive: an animated fantasy UI running live in Unity
author: _AssetSmithy_
selftext:
Hi everyone! My earlier UI kits were plain sprite sets - frames, buttons and panels without any animation or effects, and the previews were just as simple. This time I wanted the whole UI to come alive.  
  
This is Arcane, the first style of my Animated Fantasy UI Kit: dark slate, silver filigree, glowing runes and violet crystals. The video is recorded straight from the running demo in Unity - every effect runs live, none of it is added in editing.  
  
**What's in it:**  
\- 45 menus, from main menu, settings and brightness check to inventory, crafting, enchanting, skill tree, world map, quest journal, shop, HUD, combat, save/load and credits  
\- Every screen animates in, every button and slot reacts on hover  
\- Effects with a job: a rune circle whose crystal swings to the hovered entry, a hanging map scroll that drops and unrolls, an anvil strike with sparks and steam, a spark that runs along the constellation line when you learn a skill, crystals that orbit and enchant a sword, a stone book whose pages turn in real 3D  
\- Backgrounds that move: torches and candles, volumetric clouds, light shafts, aurora, waving banners  
\- 65 animation scripts and 25 shaders on Unity's standard UI (uGUI), Unity 6  
  
**How I made it:**  
The artwork is AI-generated with Gemini/Flow and then reworked in Photoshop (cutouts, cleanup, consistent colors across all menus). Every script and shader was written by Claude Code. I set the direction, checked every screen and gave feedback until it held up.  
  
Two more styles are on the way: a dragon forge look in blackened steel with glowing lava cracks, and a celestial one in white marble with gold and moonsilver. Each style gets all 45 menus.  
  
Any feedback is very welcome.

comments.author: biggdogg420
comments.body: The skill-tree spark has a clear job: it tells you which node just unlocked. Does the selection state still read in a reduced-motion mode? I’d keep the unlocked node’s final highlight and drop the travelling effect so players can get the same information with less movement.

replies.author: _AssetSmithy_
replies.body: Yes, the state still reads: the learned star stays lit and its links keep glowing, the spark is only the transition. Every effect in the kit is its own component, so a reduced-motion setting in the game can simply switch the travelling effects off and keep the highlights.

comments.author: BeltwayBro
comments.body: This turned out really cool! Can you share your v1 static art so we can see the starting baseline? Or was this an entirely new system?

replies.author: _AssetSmithy_
replies.body: Thanks! It's an entirely new system: new art, new menu layouts, and every motion runs live in Unity (scripts and shaders), nothing is a pre-rendered video. My earlier kits were fully static, so there's no v1 of this one.
